definition: Anonymized identifier of the student who worked on the problem.
calculation_or_categories: Integer ID.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Primary grouping key for longitudinal student modeling. Treat as categorical/identifier, not continuous numeric data.
model_use_notes: Retain for ordering, grouping, joining, auditing, and evaluation only.
documentation_basis: Official documentation

definition: Chronological identifier for the original problem log. Lower values generally correspond to earlier logged interactions.
calculation_or_categories: Unique integer in this collapsed file.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Useful for ordering a student’s interactions because the dataset has no absolute response timestamp. Do not assume equal differences in order_id represent equal elapsed time.
model_use_notes: Retain for ordering, grouping, joining, auditing, and evaluation only.
documentation_basis: Official documentation + observed file

definition: Human-readable name of the skill associated with the problem.
calculation_or_categories: Examples include Equation Solving Two or Fewer Steps, Proportion, Box and Whisker. Blank values occur.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: The collapsed file may contain composite skill_id values even when skill_name shows one readable label; use skill_id as the more reliable machine key.
model_use_notes: Use the Skill_* indicators instead; retain skill_name only for reporting and interpretation.
documentation_basis: Official documentation + observed file

definition: Unique row identifier present in the corrected collapsed CSV. This field is not described on the official Combined Dataset column page.
calculation_or_categories: Unique integer in this file; values are not consecutive.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Treat as a file-level row key, not as student chronology. Use order_id for chronological ordering.
model_use_notes: Retain for ordering, grouping, joining, auditing, and evaluation only.
documentation_basis: Observed in downloaded CSV; not officially documented

definition: Identifier of the assignment instance. An assignment is specific to a teacher/class, while the same problem set (sequence_id) may be assigned in multiple assignments.
calculation_or_categories: Integer ID.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Mostly contextual metadata. Do not use as a numeric magnitude.
model_use_notes: Exclude from the baseline to reduce memorization, identity dependence, and weak generalization; revisit only in a controlled experiment.
documentation_basis: Official documentation

definition: Identifier of the ASSISTment. An ASSISTment is an instructional item that can contain a main problem and, when applicable, scaffolding problems.
calculation_or_categories: Integer ID.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Multiple problem_id values can belong to the same ASSISTment.
model_use_notes: Exclude from the baseline to reduce memorization, identity dependence, and weak generalization; revisit only in a controlled experiment.
documentation_basis: Official documentation

definition: Identifier of the specific problem presented to the student.
calculation_or_categories: Integer ID.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Treat as categorical/identifier. A problem can be encountered by many students.
model_use_notes: Exclude from the baseline to reduce memorization, identity dependence, and weak generalization; revisit only in a controlled experiment.
documentation_basis: Official documentation

definition: Indicates whether the row is the main/original problem or a scaffolding problem.
calculation_or_categories: 1 = main/original problem; 0 = scaffolding problem.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: For a clean next-problem correctness model, it is often reasonable to begin with original = 1 and analyze scaffolding separately.
model_use_notes: The filtered dataset contains only original = 1, so this column has no predictive variance.
documentation_basis: Official documentation

definition: Number of answer attempts the student made on this problem.
calculation_or_categories: Nonnegative count.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: The downloaded file contains some 0 values and a very large maximum, so inspect/outlier-handle before modeling.
model_use_notes: Observed during or after the response being predicted. Use only its leakage-safe historical aggregates where available.
documentation_basis: Official detailed interpretation + observed file

definition: Time from problem start until the student’s first action, measured in milliseconds. The first action may be an answer attempt or a request for help.
calculation_or_categories: Milliseconds.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: The actual CSV contains negative and extremely large values, indicating data-quality issues. Do not use raw without validation, clipping/winsorization, or exclusion rules.
model_use_notes: Observed during or after the response being predicted. Use only its leakage-safe historical aggregates where available.
documentation_basis: Official documentation + observed file

definition: Mode in which the problem was delivered.
calculation_or_categories: Observed in this file: tutor, test. Older documentation also mentions pre-test/post-test modes, but they are not present here.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Use observed categories from this CSV rather than assuming all categories listed in older documentation exist.
model_use_notes: Exclude from the initial numeric feature matrix; one-hot encode inside a later pipeline if validation justifies it.
documentation_basis: Official documentation + observed file

definition: Format used for the student response.
calculation_or_categories: Observed: algebra = math-evaluated text response; choose_1 = single-choice multiple choice; fill_in_1 = fill-in text/string response; choose_n = select-multiple response; open_response = open response.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: The official older page says fill_in, but the actual corrected collapsed file uses fill_in_1. choose_n is also present although not listed on that page.
model_inclusion: Exclude — raw categorical replaced by one-hot
model_use_notes: Use the answer_type_* indicator columns in numeric model inputs.
documentation_basis: Official documentation reconciled to observed file

definition: Identifier for the problem set (historically called a sequence). Different assignments can reference the same sequence_id.
calculation_or_categories: Integer ID.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Content-level identifier; treat as categorical.
model_use_notes: Exclude from the baseline to reduce memorization, identity dependence, and weak generalization; revisit only in a controlled experiment.
documentation_basis: Official documentation

definition: Identifier of the class associated with the student/assignment.
calculation_or_categories: Integer ID.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Contextual identifier. Treat as categorical and avoid interpreting its numeric magnitude.
model_use_notes: Exclude from the baseline to reduce memorization, identity dependence, and weak generalization; revisit only in a controlled experiment.
documentation_basis: Official documentation

definition: Position of the assignment on the class assignments page.
calculation_or_categories: Positive integer.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: This is assignment-page position, not the student’s within-problem response order.
model_use_notes: Known before the current response; include as a candidate input and confirm value through validation ablation.
documentation_basis: Official documentation

definition: Identifier of the original problem set when a sequence has been copied; otherwise it may equal sequence_id.
calculation_or_categories: Integer ID.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Useful for grouping copied versions of the same underlying problem set.
model_use_notes: Exclude from the baseline to reduce memorization, identity dependence, and weak generalization; revisit only in a controlled experiment.
documentation_basis: Official documentation

definition: Anonymized identifier of the teacher who assigned the problem.
calculation_or_categories: Integer ID.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Contextual identifier; not needed for a student-skill proficiency project unless explicitly modeling teacher/class effects.
model_use_notes: Exclude from the baseline to reduce memorization, identity dependence, and weak generalization; revisit only in a controlled experiment.
documentation_basis: Official documentation

definition: Anonymized identifier of the school where the problem was assigned.
calculation_or_categories: Integer ID.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Contextual identifier; treat as categorical, not continuous.
model_use_notes: Exclude from the baseline to reduce memorization, identity dependence, and weak generalization; revisit only in a controlled experiment.
documentation_basis: Official documentation

definition: Number of hints the student requested while working on the problem.
calculation_or_categories: Count from 0 upward; observed range in this file is 0–10.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: The older 2009–10 page contains a wording error that describes this as attempts; the more detailed ASSISTments interpretation page clearly defines it as hints requested.
model_use_notes: Observed during or after the response being predicted. Use only its leakage-safe historical aggregates where available.
documentation_basis: Official detailed interpretation + observed file

definition: Total number of hints available for the problem.
calculation_or_categories: Count; observed range in this file is 0–10.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Can be used with hint_count to derive a fraction of available hints used. A value of 0 means no hints were available/defined.
model_use_notes: Known before the current response; include as a candidate input and confirm value through validation ablation.
documentation_basis: Official detailed interpretation + observed file

definition: Intended estimate of total time the student spent completing the problem, in milliseconds, including time across attempts/hints.
calculation_or_categories: Milliseconds.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: ASSISTments explicitly warns this field is often computed incorrectly. The uploaded file also contains negative and extreme values; treat it as noisy and validate before use.
model_use_notes: Observed during or after the response being predicted. Use only its leakage-safe historical aggregates where available.
documentation_basis: Official detailed interpretation + observed file

definition: Identifier of the ASSISTment template. ASSISTments sharing a template_id have similar/templated questions.
calculation_or_categories: Integer ID.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Potential way to group structurally similar questions. Treat as categorical.
model_use_notes: Exclude from the baseline to reduce memorization, identity dependence, and weak generalization; revisit only in a controlled experiment.
documentation_basis: Official documentation

definition: Type of the student’s first action after opening the problem.
calculation_or_categories: 0 = answer attempt; 1 = hint request; 2 = scaffolding / break problem into steps.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: The Combined page only loosely describes attempt vs hint; the detailed interpretation page documents the scaffolding code 2, which is present in this file.
model_use_notes: Observed during or after the response being predicted. Use only its leakage-safe historical aggregates where available.
documentation_basis: Official detailed interpretation + observed file

definition: Indicates whether the student requested the final “bottom-out” hint, which generally reveals the answer.
calculation_or_categories: 1 = requested bottom-out hint; 0 = used hinting but did not request bottom-out hint; literal NA = no hint was requested / not applicable.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Read as categorical/string rather than numeric because this CSV uses the literal NA marker. Scaffolding questions cannot receive hints.
model_use_notes: Observed during or after the response being predicted. Use only its leakage-safe historical aggregates where available.
documentation_basis: Official detailed interpretation + observed file

definition: Count of opportunities the student has had to practice the associated skill up to and including this interaction, as supplied by the dataset.
calculation_or_categories: Positive integer count.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Highly relevant to knowledge/proficiency modeling. In this collapsed file a student-problem has one row even when skill_id is composite, so interpret the supplied count as the dataset’s collapsed opportunity value rather than reconstructing per-skill counts from this field alone.
model_use_notes: Prefer for tree models; compare against log1p_opportunity for linear models rather than automatically using both.
documentation_basis: Official documentation + corrected-file structure

definition: Whether the student was correct on the first attempt. In Skill Builder assignments, requesting tutoring (a hint or “Break this Problem Into Steps”) causes the problem to be marked incorrect.
calculation_or_categories: 1 = correct on first attempt; 0 = incorrect on first attempt or requested help.
data_quality_and_leakage_notes: Common prediction target. Because help-seeking can force correct=0, it represents independent first-attempt success rather than final eventual correctness.
model_use_notes: Binary prediction target; never include it in the input feature matrix.
documentation_basis: Official documentation
